title: Arecanut — Harvest Timing, Processing and Storage
content:
ARECANUT HARVEST:

FIRST HARVEST: 3rd year after planting. Full economic yield from 8-10 years.

HARVEST FREQUENCY:
- Monthly or bi-monthly bunch harvest.
- Tender green nuts (green chali): Harvest at 7-8 months after flower opening.
- Ripe nuts (red arecanut): Harvest at 9-10 months — fully ripe, yellow-orange.

MATURITY INDICATORS:
- Green chali: Tender, flesh milky white, easy to cut.
- Ripe nut: Yellow-orange color, longitudinal lines appear, 3-5 cm size.
- Dried red arecanut: Deep red color after sun drying.

HARVEST METHOD:
- Climbing irons (traditional): Farmer climbs using iron loops.
- Hydraulic platform for tall palms (>12m).
- Long bamboo pole with knife attachment (Kavli) for dwarfs.

PROCESSING TYPES:
1. GREEN CHALI (Kallu adike):
- Harvest young green nuts.
- Remove husk (fresh).
- Boil in water for 2-3 hours.
- Sun dry 4-5 weeks to chali stage.

2. DRIED RED ARECANUT (Gota adike):
- Harvest fully ripe nuts.
- Sun dry with husk for 35-40 days.
- Remove husk after drying.
- Final moisture: 12%.

3. RIPE CURED (Rashi adike):
- Traditional fermentation method of coastal Karnataka.

STORAGE:
- Chali: Store in moisture-proof bags at 10-12% moisture.
- Red arecanut: Fumigate periodically.
- Avoid storage > 18°C — prone to mold at high humidity.

YIELD: Fully mature garden: 2.5-3.5 t/ha dried nuts. 8-10 kg/palm/year average.
